findings.title: Documented preset roles understate their effective privileges
findings.description: The page states that `admin` cannot manage the collaborator roster and recommends it when the grantee must not add collaborators. It also says `developer` has only build/deploy powers and no data access. The owning platform source currently defines `admin` as every capability except app deletion and transfer, which includes `access:manage`, and defines `developer` with `analytics:view`. An operator following this page can therefore give an untrusted administrator delegation authority or expose per-user analytics to an agent while believing those powers were excluded. An admin can add collaborators with policy, function, billing, or other significant capabilities.
findings.recommendation: Make the documented matrix match the authoritative access-model implementation and add a contract test that compares every documented preset with the source capability bundle. Explicitly warn that the current admin role can manage collaborators and that developer includes analytics access. If those powers are not intended, remove them from the implementation instead.

findings.title: Bridge example permits anonymous updates when author is null
findings.description: The bridge update rule compares `@user.id` with `@data.author` without first requiring authentication or declaring `author` as required and immutable. An unauthenticated caller has a null user id, so a legacy, malformed, or optional-schema post whose author is missing or null satisfies the owner branch through `null == null`. The read-only control-plane admin projection does not mitigate this bypass because the first branch already authorizes the update.
findings.recommendation: Require `@user.id != null` around both branches, declare `author` required, bind it to the authenticated user on create, and preserve it on update. For example: `@user.id != null && (@user.id == @data.author || get(/__admins__/@user.id) != null)`.

findings.title: Founder remains a permanent admin-minting authority after revocation
findings.description: The admin-create rule permanently authorizes any request whose caller equals `FOUNDER`; it does not constrain the target `$userId` to the founder and has no one-time or empty-registry condition. This contradicts the claim that `active: false` is a complete off-switch. After an active admin deactivates a compromised founder row, the founder credential can create an active row for another attacker-controlled account and regain every admin-gated power. The authorityClosure attestation accepts the founder as an exception but does not make that exception one-time.
findings.recommendation: Either document `FOUNDER` as a permanent, non-revocable admin minter or constrain bootstrap creation to the founder's own row, such as `@user.id == @const.FOUNDER && $userId == @const.FOUNDER`. Preserve the existing active-admin branch for later promotions and test that a deactivated founder cannot create another admin.
